metadata.query: What happened between Verstappen and Hamilton at Turn 4 during the 2021 Brazilian GP?

data.query: What happened between Verstappen and Hamilton at Turn 4 during the 2021 Brazilian GP?
data.summary:
During the **2021 Brazilian Grand Prix (São Paulo GP)** on **November 14, 2021**, a highly controversial on-track duel occurred between championship rivals Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen at Turn 4 [1.5, 1.7]:

### 1. The Incident (Lap 48)
On **Lap 48**, Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) utilized DRS down the back straight to pull alongside and slightly ahead of race leader Max Verstappen (Red Bull Racing) on the outside line entering Turn 4 [1.2, 1.10]. Defending his position, Verstappen braked exceptionally late on the inside [1.10, 1.4]. This sent his car deep into the corner, forcing both himself and Hamilton completely off the track onto the asphalt run-off area [1.2, 1.10]. No physical contact was made, and Verstappen retained the lead [1.3, 1.4]. 

### 2. The Stewards' Decision and Controversy
The FIA stewards noted the incident but determined that no formal investigation was necessary, choosing to let them race [1.3, 1.7]. Controversy erupted when F1 Race Director Michael Masi revealed that the stewards did not have access to the forward-facing onboard camera footage from Verstappen’s car at the time of their decision, relying solely on broadcast feeds [1.1, 1.7]. 

### 3. "Right of Review" and Regulations
On **November 16, 2021**, after the missing onboard footage was publicly released, Mercedes officially petitioned the FIA for a **"Right of Review"** under **Article 14.1.1 of the International Sporting Code (ISC)** [1.9, 1.10]. This regulation allows stewards to reopen a case if a "significant and relevant new element" is discovered that was unavailable at the time [1.7]. On **November 19, 2021**, the stewards rejected the appeal, stating the footage did not represent a significant enough factor to change their original decision [1.2, 1.3].

### 4. Key Quotes
* **Max Verstappen** defended his actions: *"I don't expect [any punishment] to happen because I thought it was hard and fair racing between two drivers that are fighting for the title."* [1.3, 1.4]
* **Toto Wolff (Mercedes Team Principal)** criticized the initial lack of investigation, calling the stewards' decision *"laughable."* [1.2, 1.3]

### 5. Resolution
The on-track dispute ended up having no impact on the race result. Hamilton regrouped, caught Verstappen again, and executed a clean, decisive overtake for the lead at Turn 4 on **Lap 59** to win the Grand Prix [1.2, 1.4].
